Lists Gary Paul Gershmann's Hamiltonian Ideals and the Bill of Rights as a 1992 Duke University PhD dissertation.

basis: The reviewer at Nova Southeastern earned a history PhD at Duke, where the dissertation on the other key was submitted. The matching institution and degree support the identification; the bibliography spells the dissertation author's surname Gershmann.

evidence.says: Tyndale's history faculty includes Gary Miedema, who earned a PhD at Queen's University in 2000.
Gary R. Miedema wrote Canada's Sake, a PhD dissertation at Queen's University in 2000.
Gary Richard Miedema authored For Canada's Sake; its author note identifies him as a research associate at Emmanuel College, University of Toronto.

basis: The Tyndale historian's Queen's PhD year matches the dissertation of Gary R. Miedema, whose name and dissertation title connect him to the book author identified with the Emmanuel College research centre. This links the two review affiliations through a documented degree and work.

evidence.says: Aethlon's memorial identifies Glynn Arthur Leyshon as a University of Western Ontario professor of anatomy and kinesiology until retirement in 1996.
Contemporary Authors attributes the H-Net review of Parallel Lines and the Hockey Universe to Glynn A. Leyshon.

basis: Both review credits identify Glynn A. Leyshon with the University of Western Ontario in 2000–2003; one specifies its emeritus professor of kinesiology. The Aethlon memorial confirms that career, supporting the institutional match to the 2001 review as a strong inference.

evidence.says: Lists Lauren Ann Kattner's Ethnicity Plus as a 1997 Ph.D. dissertation at the University of Texas at Austin.

basis: The dissertation is attributed to Lauren Ann Kattner, the full name on the review key. I found no source tying the reviewer or the review to the dissertation author or her institution, so the shared name alone does not establish identity.

evidence.says: The 2003 review of P Sanat Kültür Antika is credited to Burcu Dogramaci, Hamburg.
The 2003 review of Lotte Laserstein is credited to Burcu Dogramaci, Institut für Kunstgeschichte, LMU München.

basis: The review pages identify the authors by the same name, but do not establish a link between the two reviews or a shared institution at the relevant time.

evidence.says: Mark D. Van Ells's CV lists his 1995 review of Wisconsin's Ethnic Settlement Trail and his 1996 H-PCAACA review of The Fire Within.

basis: Van Ells's university-hosted CV lists the review on key a and a review on key b under the same author.

evidence.says: Gonzaga lists Theodore Nitz in its history faculty with a Washington State Ph.D. from 1999.
Duke University Press attributes a review of German Colonialism in a Global Age to Theodore Nitz in H-Diplo.

basis: The sources support the Gonzaga career and 2015 review on side b, but I found no source connecting the 2004 review on side a to that career or to the other review. The shared name and subject alone do not establish identity.

evidence.says: Roger E. Hedlund reviewed The South Indian Pentecostal Movement in the Twentieth Century for H-Pentecostalism in September 2008.
Roger E. Hedlund reviewed Strong Religion, Zealous Media for H-Pentecostalism in August 2009.

basis: The review records confirm the same name and publication venue, but no source found ties both reviews to one person. The shared subject and name alone do not establish identity under the review criteria.

evidence.says: H-Net credits Kathryn Brammall with the November 2008 review of Marvelous Protestantism; its page source identifies her with Truman State University.

basis: The 2008 review on key a identifies its reviewer with Truman State University, the affiliation recorded for key b. The institution and date support a single career.

evidence.says: Christa Salamandra's CV lists the 2008 H-Net review of Among the Jasmine Trees and a Lehman College professorship from 2017.
The 2025 article Hosting as Ethic and Method names Christa Salamandra of Lehman College and the CUNY Graduate Center and gives ORCID 0000-0002-7269-1694.

basis: The reviewer’s CV places her at Lehman College in the period of the 2025 article, whose author has the same affiliation and the ORCID on the other key. This supports one career across both works.

evidence.says: H-Soz-Kult credits Alexander Cammann with the review of Ulrich Mählert's Kleine Geschichte der DDR, published 15 May 1999.

basis: Both keys credit the same May 1999 H-Soz-u-Kult review of Kleine Geschichte der DDR. The publisher identifies Alexander Cammann as its reviewer, providing a direct shared-work link.

evidence.says: Stefan Gunther of Brandeis University reviewed Politik mit der Erinnerung in 1998.
Stefan Gunther earned a Brandeis PhD in English and American Literature in 2000 and worked at Johns Hopkins University.

basis: The 1998 review identifies Gunther at Brandeis; the Kent biography links a Brandeis doctorate in 2000 to a career at Johns Hopkins, the institution credited on the 2004 review. The matching institutional career supports the identity, though the biography does not date the Johns Hopkins appointment or list the reviews.

evidence.says: The 1997 review of Der verwaltete Körper names Maria Mesner of the Renner-Institut as reviewer.
The 2002 review of Mutter ledig - Vater Staat names Maria Mesner of the Institut für Zeitgeschichte, Universität Wien, as reviewer.
Maria Mesner's CV lists work at the Renner-Institut in 1987–1999 and teaching at Vienna's history and contemporary history institutes since 1997.

basis: The two reviews identify reviewers at institutions that Maria Mesner's university CV places her at in the relevant years. The matching dated affiliations link the two credits to the same career.
